issues.description: The problem specification and the template define a public method named singFarmSong() in Farm that should print the song, but the solution implements this functionality in a method named playFarmSong() instead of singFarmSong(). This name/signature mismatch between the expected API (singFarmSong) and the solution (playFarmSong) is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students and break automated tests or examples that call singFarmSong().
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name in the solution with the problem/template by renaming playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() in the solution that delegates to playFarmSong(). Ensure the public API matches the problem statement and template so students and tests can call singFarmSong().

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a Farm.singFarmSong() method (the exercise asks students to implement singFarmSong()), but the solution implementation provides a method named playFarmSong() instead. This naming divergence for the same conceptual behavior (playing/singing the farm song) creates a direct mapping confusion: students looking for the reference implementation or comparing against the solution will not find singFarmSong(), and automated checks or graders referencing singFarmSong() may fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a singFarmSong() method that delegates to playFarmSong(), so the solution matches the problem statement and template API.
